claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000340.summary: On domain controllers, the "Access this computer from the network" right may be held only by Administrators, Authenticated Users, and Enterprise Domain Controllers; any other account or group must be removed unless an application is documented with the ISSO as needing it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000340.caution: Removing a group that an application service account relies on will break that application's network access to the domain controller; review vendor documentation before trimming the list.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000350.summary: On domain controllers, only the Administrators group may hold the "Add workstations to domain" right, so ordinary users cannot join computers to the domain on their own.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000350.caution: Help-desk or provisioning accounts that currently join machines to the domain will lose that ability unless they are members of Administrators or given delegated permissions another way.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000360.summary: On domain controllers, only the Administrators group may be granted "Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services", so no one else can open a Remote Desktop session to a domain controller.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000360.caution: Anyone who currently uses Remote Desktop to reach the domain controller without being in Administrators will lose access.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000370.summary: On domain controllers, the Guests group must be listed under "Deny access to this computer from the network", so guest accounts can never connect to a domain controller over the network.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000380.summary: On domain controllers, the Guests group must be listed under "Deny log on as a batch job", so guest accounts cannot run scheduled tasks or other batch jobs on a domain controller.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000390.summary: On domain controllers, the "Deny log on as a service" right must contain no accounts or groups at all, because denying service logon on a domain controller could stop legitimate directory and system services from starting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000391.summary: Domain controllers must enforce strong certificate binding in the Kerberos KDC (StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement set to 1 or 2), so a certificate used for logon is tied firmly to the right account and cannot be spoofed onto another one.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000391.caution: Certificates issued before strong mapping was available may fail authentication under full enforcement (value 2); confirm certificates carry the new mapping or start with compatibility mode (value 1).

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000400.summary: On domain controllers, the Guests group must be listed under "Deny log on locally", so guest accounts can never sign in at the console of a domain controller.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000401.summary: On domain controllers, enable the KDC policy "Allow name-based strong mappings for certificates" so that certificate logons can be matched to accounts using strong name-based mappings rather than weak ones that can be spoofed.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000401.caution: The policy interacts with the KDC strong certificate binding enforcement setting; test certificate logons after enabling it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000410.summary: On domain controllers, the Guests group must be listed under "Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services", so guest accounts can never open a Remote Desktop session to a domain controller.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000420.summary: On domain controllers, only the Administrators group may hold the "Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation" right, because whoever has it can let accounts impersonate users to other services.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000430.summary: The password of the krbtgt account, which signs every Kerberos ticket in the domain, must be reset at least every 180 days (and changed twice to clear the old password from history) so a stolen copy cannot be used to forge tickets indefinitely.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000430.caution: Changing the password twice in rapid succession forces every client and application service to reauthenticate; change it once, wait for replication to finish, then change it again unless a compromise is suspected.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000020.summary: On domain-joined member servers, enable "Apply UAC restrictions to local accounts on network logons" so that local administrator accounts get a filtered token over the network and cannot be used to run with full admin rights remotely.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000020.caution: Network scanning tools that authenticate with local administrator accounts may fail; use domain accounts for scans, and the SecGuide custom templates must be installed before the policy appears.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000030.summary: On domain-joined member servers, disable "Enumerate local users on domain-joined computers" so the logon screen does not list local account names for anyone to see.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000040.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, enable "Restrict Unauthenticated RPC clients" with "Authenticated" selected, so anonymous callers cannot connect to the RPC service and probe or abuse it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000040.caution: Applications that make anonymous RPC calls to the server will be refused after this change.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000050.summary: On domain-joined member servers, limit the number of previous domain logons that Windows caches to 4 or fewer, so that fewer stored password hashes are available to an attacker who gets hold of the machine.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000050.caution: If a domain controller is unreachable, only the last four users who logged on can still sign in with cached credentials.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000060.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, restrict remote calls to the Security Account Manager so that only Administrators can query local account and group information over the network, denying attackers an easy way to enumerate accounts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000060.caution: Applications that remotely read local account information with non-administrator credentials will break; such an exception must be documented and approved by the ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000070.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, the "Access this computer from the network" right may be held only by Administrators and Authenticated Users; remove any other account or group unless an application is documented with the ISSO as requiring it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000070.caution: Removing a group that an application service account depends on will cut off that application's network access; check vendor documentation first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000080.summary: On member servers, the "Deny access to this computer from the network" right must include Enterprise Admins, Domain Admins, local accounts (or local accounts in Administrators), and Guests, so highly privileged domain credentials and local admin accounts cannot be used to reach the server over the network.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000080.caution: Denying "Local account" can break failover clustering and any process that uses local accounts over the network, and denying Domain Admins can block administrators who manage the server remotely with those accounts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000090.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, the "Deny log on as a batch job" right must include Guests, and on domain-joined systems also Enterprise Admins and Domain Admins, so guest accounts and the most privileged domain accounts cannot be used to run scheduled tasks or batch jobs on the server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000090.caution: Any scheduled task that currently runs under a Domain Admins or Enterprise Admins account will stop running; move those tasks to a less privileged service account first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000100.summary: On domain-joined member servers, the "Deny log on as a service" right must contain exactly Enterprise Admins and Domain Admins (and nothing at all on nondomain-joined systems), so services on ordinary servers cannot run under the most privileged domain accounts.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000100.caution: Any Windows service configured to run as a Domain Admins or Enterprise Admins account will fail to start after this change; reassign such services to dedicated service accounts first.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000110.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, the "Deny log on locally" right must include Guests, and on domain-joined systems also Enterprise Admins and Domain Admins, so the most privileged domain accounts and guests cannot sign in at the console of an ordinary server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000110.caution: Administrators who habitually sign in to member servers with a Domain Admins account will be refused at the console and need a separate, less privileged administrative account.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000120.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, the "Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services" right must include Guests, and on domain-joined systems also Enterprise Admins, Domain Admins, and the built-in Local account group, so those accounts cannot open Remote Desktop sessions to ordinary servers.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000120.caution: Denying Domain Admins and all local accounts can cut off the only way some staff currently reach the server via Remote Desktop; make sure a permitted domain account with the needed rights exists before applying it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-MS-000130.summary: On member servers and standalone systems, the "Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation" right must be defined but left empty, because no one on an ordinary server should be able to configure accounts to impersonate users to other services.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-PK-000010.summary: The DoD Root CA 3, 4, 5, and 6 certificates must be present in the local machine Trusted Root Certification Authorities store, with the listed thumbprints, so the server trusts certificates issued by the DoD PKI for smart card logon, signing, and encrypted connections.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-PK-000010.caution: Confirm the thumbprints match the listed values; installing a root certificate with the wrong thumbprint would make the server trust an unknown authority.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-PK-000020.summary: On unclassified systems, the DoD Interoperability Root CA 2 cross-certificate for DoD Root CA 3 must be placed in the local machine Untrusted Certificates store, so certificate chains do not resolve through the interoperability root to external bridge authorities.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-PK-000020.caution: The FBCA Cross-Certificate Removal Tool must be run both as an administrator and as the current user, otherwise the cross-certificate may remain trusted for user sessions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-PK-000030.summary: On unclassified systems, the US DoD CCEB Interoperability Root CA 2 cross-certificates for DoD Root CA 3 and DoD Root CA 6 must be placed in the local machine Untrusted Certificates store, so certificate chains cannot be built through the CCEB interoperability root.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-PK-000030.caution: The FBCA Cross-Certificate Removal Tool must be run both as an administrator and as the current user, or the cross-certificate may still be trusted in user sessions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000010.summary: The built-in Guest account must be disabled ("Accounts: Guest account status" set to Disabled), so nobody can sign in without a real, individually accountable account.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000030.summary: Rename the built-in Administrator account to something other than "Administrator", so attackers cannot rely on the well-known account name when guessing credentials.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000030.caution: Scripts or documentation that reference the account by the name "Administrator" will need updating.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000040.summary: Rename the built-in Guest account to something other than "Guest", so the well-known account name is not available to attackers even though the account should also be disabled.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000050.summary: Enable the "Force audit policy subcategory settings to override audit policy category settings" option, so the detailed advanced audit policy subcategories actually take effect instead of being overridden by the older, coarser category settings.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000050.caution: Once enabled, only the advanced audit subcategory settings apply, so any auditing that was configured only through the legacy categories stops being collected until it is set at the subcategory level.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000060.summary: Enable "Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always)" so that all traffic on the secure channel between this server and its domain controllers is always signed or encrypted, preventing tampering or eavesdropping on authentication traffic.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000060.caution: If a domain controller cannot sign or encrypt secure channel traffic, the server will be unable to authenticate to the domain.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000070.summary: Enable "Domain member: Digitally encrypt secure channel data (when possible)" so the server encrypts its secure channel to domain controllers whenever the domain controller supports it, keeping authentication traffic private.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000080.summary: Enable "Domain member: Digitally sign secure channel data (when possible)" so the server signs its secure channel traffic to domain controllers whenever they support it, making tampering detectable.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000090.summary: Keep "Domain member: Disable machine account password changes" set to Disabled, so the server continues to change its own computer account password on schedule instead of keeping the same credential indefinitely.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000100.summary: Set "Domain member: Maximum machine account password age" to 30 days or less (never 0), so the server's computer account password is rotated regularly; 30 days is already the default.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000100.caution: A value of 0 disables password changes entirely and is not acceptable.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000110.summary: Enable "Domain member: Require strong (Windows 2000 or later) session key" so the server insists on a strong encryption key for its secure channel with domain controllers.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000110.caution: If this setting is not configured consistently across systems, a server may be unable to join the domain.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000120.summary: Set "Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit" to 900 seconds (15 minutes) or less, but not 0, so an unattended session locks itself with the screen saver and cannot be used by a passerby.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000120.caution: A value of 0 effectively disables the lock and does not satisfy the requirement.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000130.summary: Configure the "Message text for users attempting to log on" security option with the required U.S. Government warning banner, so everyone who logs on at the console is told the system is monitored and consents to those conditions.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000130.caution: The banner text must match the required wording exactly, or the check will still fail.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000150.summary: Set "Interactive logon: Smart card removal behavior" to Lock Workstation or Force Logoff, so pulling the smart card out of the reader immediately locks or ends the session instead of leaving it open.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000150.caution: On servers this can terminate users' remote sessions; if that causes problems, an organizational policy for manually locking unattended sessions may be used instead but must be documented with the ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000160.summary: Enable "Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always)" so this server, when acting as an SMB client, always signs its file-sharing traffic and refuses connections that cannot be signed, blocking tampering and relay attacks.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000160.caution: Connections to file servers or devices that do not support SMB signing will fail once signing is required.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000170.summary: Enable "Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees)" so the server, as an SMB client, signs its file-sharing traffic whenever the remote server supports it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000180.summary: Disable "Microsoft Network Client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers" so the server never sends a plain-text password to a non-Microsoft file server where it could be captured on the network.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000180.caution: Very old third-party SMB servers that only accept plain-text passwords will no longer be reachable.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000190.summary: Enable "Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)" so this server always signs the SMB file-sharing traffic it serves and rejects clients that cannot sign, blocking tampering and relay attacks.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000190.caution: Clients and devices that cannot perform SMB signing will lose access to this server's shares.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000200.summary: Enable "Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees)" so the server signs SMB file-sharing traffic whenever the connecting client supports it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000240.summary: Disable "Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users" so that anonymous connections are not treated as members of the Everyone group and cannot inherit whatever access Everyone has been granted.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000260.summary: Enable "Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM" so services running as Local System authenticate with the computer's own account when NTLM is used, rather than falling back to an anonymous connection.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000270.summary: Disable "Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback" so that NTLM authentication attempts by Local System services never fall back to an unauthenticated null session with no credentials at all.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000280.summary: Disable "Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities" so that people cannot authenticate to the server with consumer online accounts instead of domain or local accounts.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000290.summary: Configure the allowed Kerberos encryption types to only AES128_HMAC_SHA1, AES256_HMAC_SHA1, and Future encryption types, so the weak DES and RC4 ciphers can no longer be used for Kerberos tickets on this server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000290.caution: Domain trusts to older domain controllers that still rely on RC4 may break unless "The other domain supports Kerberos AES Encryption" is selected on the trust.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000320.summary: Set "Network security: LDAP client signing requirements" to at least "Negotiate signing" so the server's LDAP client asks directory servers to sign traffic when they can, protecting directory queries from tampering.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000330.summary: Set the minimum session security for NTLM SSP-based clients to require both NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption, so this server never negotiates a weaker NTLM session when it connects to other systems.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000330.caution: Connections to servers that only support older NTLM session security or 56-bit encryption will fail.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000340.summary: Set the minimum session security for NTLM SSP-based servers to require both NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption, so clients connecting to this server cannot negotiate a weaker NTLM session.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000340.caution: Legacy clients that cannot do NTLMv2 session security with 128-bit encryption will be refused.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000350.summary: Set "System cryptography: Force strong key protection for user keys stored on the computer" so users must enter a password each time they use a private key stored on the server, preventing a stolen key from being used silently.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000350.caution: Any process that uses a user's stored private key without an interactive session will be blocked by the password prompt.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000360.summary: Enable "System cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing" so Windows only uses validated cryptographic algorithms; this does not apply to servers hosting SharePoint.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000360.caution: Systems with FIPS mode enabled cannot communicate over encrypted or signed protocols with servers that do not support those algorithms, and both browser and web server must use TLS or secure sites will not load.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000380.summary: Enable "User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account" so even the built-in Administrator runs with a filtered token and must approve elevation; this does not apply to Server Core installations.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000380.caution: Tasks run under the built-in Administrator account will start prompting for elevation.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000390.summary: Disable "Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop" so accessibility applications cannot bypass the protected elevation prompt that keeps other programs from faking or intercepting it; not applicable to Server Core.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000400.summary: Set the UAC elevation prompt for administrators to "Prompt for consent on the secure desktop" (or the stricter "Prompt for credentials on the secure desktop"), so administrators are always asked on an isolated desktop before anything runs elevated; not applicable to Server Core.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000410.summary: Set the UAC elevation prompt for standard users to "Automatically deny elevation requests", so a non-administrator cannot be tricked or coaxed into supplying admin credentials to elevate a program; not applicable to Server Core.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000410.caution: Standard users who legitimately need to run something elevated will have to log on with an administrative account instead of entering credentials at a prompt.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000420.summary: Enable "User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation" so Windows notices when an installer starts and asks for administrator approval instead of letting it run silently; not applicable to Server Core.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000430.summary: Enable "User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations" so only programs installed under protected system folders can request the special UIAccess privilege; not applicable to Server Core.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000440.summary: Enable "User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode", which turns UAC on so administrators normally run with standard rights and must explicitly approve anything that needs elevation; not applicable to Server Core.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000440.caution: Turning UAC on where it was off changes how every administrator session behaves and requires a restart to fully take effect; poorly written applications that assume unfiltered admin rights may start failing.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000450.summary: Enable "User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations" so older applications that try to write to protected system areas are quietly redirected to per-user locations instead of failing or needing elevation; not applicable to Server Core.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UC-000010.summary: Windows must keep marking downloaded attachments with their origin zone; the user policy "Do not preserve zone information in file attachments" must be Not Configured or Disabled, so Windows can still warn before opening files that came from the internet.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000010.summary: The "Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller" user right must be defined but assigned to no accounts or groups, because anything holding it can read saved credentials from Credential Manager.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000030.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Allow log on locally" right, so ordinary users cannot sign in at the server console; an application account that needs it must be documented with the ISSO and supported by vendor documentation.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000030.caution: Any non-administrator who currently logs on at the console, including application service accounts, will be refused; check what needs local logon before restricting it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000040.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Back up files and directories" right, since it lets an account read every file regardless of permissions; a backup application account that needs it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000040.caution: Backup software running under a dedicated non-administrator account will stop working unless its account is documented and kept in the list.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000050.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Create a pagefile" right, so no one else can alter or replace the system paging file.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000070.summary: The "Create global objects" right may be held only by Administrators, Service, Local Service, and Network Service, so ordinary user sessions cannot create objects that affect every other session on the server; an application needing it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000070.caution: Some applications, such as those hosting sessions for multiple users, need this right for their service account and will fail without it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000080.summary: The "Create permanent shared objects" right must be defined but assigned to no accounts or groups, because it lets a process create kernel objects that other programs could be tricked into trusting.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000090.summary: Only the Administrators group (plus "NT Virtual Machine\Virtual Machines" on Hyper-V hosts) may hold the "Create symbolic links" right, because symbolic links can be used to redirect file access and trick privileged programs.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000090.caution: On Hyper-V hosts, removing the Virtual Machines entry will interfere with virtual machines; leave it in place.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000110.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Force shutdown from a remote system" right, so no other account can shut the server down over the network.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000120.summary: Only Local Service and Network Service may hold the "Generate security audits" right, so ordinary accounts cannot write fake entries into the Security log; an application needing it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000120.caution: Applications that write their own security audit events under a custom service account will lose that ability unless documented and included.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000130.summary: The "Impersonate a client after authentication" right may be held only by Administrators, Service, Local Service, and Network Service, because a process with it can act as a connected user and take on their permissions; an application needing it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000130.caution: Web servers, database engines, and similar applications often need this right for their service accounts and will break if it is stripped from them.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000140.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Increase scheduling priority" right, so no other account can starve the server of CPU by boosting its own processes; an application needing it must be documented with the ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000150.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Load and unload device drivers" right, since drivers run with full kernel access and a malicious one can take over the server.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000160.summary: The "Lock pages in memory" right must be defined but assigned to no accounts or groups, because it lets a process pin memory and starve the system; an application that requires it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000160.caution: Database servers are commonly configured to use this right for their service account; removing it without documenting the exception can hurt their performance.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000170.summary: Only the Administrators group (or an organizational Auditors group) may hold the "Manage auditing and security log" right, since it allows changing audit settings and clearing the Security log; an application needing it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000170.caution: Log collection or SIEM agents that read the Security log with a dedicated account may need this right and will stop collecting if it is removed.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000180.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Modify firmware environment values" right, so no other account can change firmware settings that affect how the server boots.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000190.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Perform volume maintenance tasks" right, since it allows low-level disk operations that could expose or destroy data.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000190.caution: Database service accounts sometimes hold this right for instant file initialization and will lose that capability.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000200.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Profile single process" right, so ordinary accounts cannot monitor the performance of processes other than their own and learn how the system is being used.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000210.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Restore files and directories" right, since it allows overwriting any file regardless of permissions; a backup application account needing it must be documented with the ISSO.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000210.caution: Backup software running under a dedicated non-administrator account will be unable to restore files unless its account is documented and kept in the list.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-UR-000220.summary: Only the Administrators group may hold the "Take ownership of files or other objects" right, since whoever owns an object can change its permissions and gain access to anything; an application needing it must be documented with the ISSO.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000180.summary: On any shared printer, standard user accounts and groups may have only the Print permission, so ordinary users cannot manage the printer or other people's print jobs; systems with no printers are not affected.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000180.caution: Do not treat "All APPLICATION PACKAGES" or "CREATOR OWNER" as standard user accounts when reviewing permissions.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000440.summary: The Windows Time service must get its time from an approved DOD source: domain-joined systems should use NT5DS to sync from the domain, while standalone systems and the PDC emulator domain controller must point their NTP client at a DOD time server, so logs and Kerberos stay in step.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000440.caution: Pointing a domain-joined system at an external NTP server instead of NT5DS, or picking a time source that is unreachable, can cause clock drift that breaks Kerberos authentication.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000460.summary: The server's firmware must be UEFI and must be running in UEFI mode rather than Legacy BIOS, as shown by "BIOS Mode" in System Information, because features such as Secure Boot depend on it; older hardware without UEFI firmware cannot meet this yet.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000460.caution: Switching an existing installation from Legacy BIOS to UEFI mode normally requires converting the disk partition layout or reinstalling; done carelessly it leaves the server unbootable.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000470.summary: Secure Boot must be turned on in the system firmware, so the server only starts boot loaders and drivers that are properly signed and rootkits cannot load before Windows; "Secure Boot State" in System Information must show "On".
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-00-000470.caution: Secure Boot requires UEFI mode and will refuse to boot unsigned or custom boot components, so confirm all drivers and boot media are signed before enabling it.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000030.summary: Set the IPv6 source routing protection level to "Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled", so an attacker cannot use source-routed packets to spoof addresses or steer traffic through the server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000030.caution: The policy only appears in Group Policy after the MSS-Legacy custom templates from the STIG package have been copied into the PolicyDefinitions directories.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000040.summary: Set the IPv4 source routing protection level to "Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled", so an attacker cannot use source-routed packets to spoof addresses or steer traffic through the server.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000040.caution: The policy only appears in Group Policy after the MSS-Legacy custom templates from the STIG package have been copied into the PolicyDefinitions directories.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000050.summary: Disable "Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes", so a forged ICMP redirect message cannot rewrite the server's routing table and divert its traffic.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000050.caution: The policy only appears in Group Policy after the MSS-Legacy custom templates from the STIG package have been installed.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000060.summary: Enable "Allow the computer to ignore NetBIOS name release requests except from WINS servers", so a malicious host cannot force the server to give up its NetBIOS name and impersonate it.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000060.caution: The policy only appears in Group Policy after the MSS-Legacy custom templates from the STIG package have been installed.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000200.summary: Enable "Turn off Inventory Collector" so the Application Compatibility Program stops gathering details about installed programs and sending them to Microsoft.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000260.summary: Set the Delivery Optimization "Download Mode" to any option except "Internet" (HTTP only, LAN, Group, Simple, or Bypass), so the server never downloads Windows updates from unknown PCs on the internet.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-CC-000320.summary: Leave File Explorer's heap termination on corruption at its default (the "Turn off heap termination on corruption" policy Not Configured or Disabled), so File Explorer shuts down when memory corruption is detected rather than continuing in an exploitable state.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000160.summary: On domain controllers, set the LDAP policy MaxConnIdleTime to 300 seconds so idle LDAP connections to the directory are dropped after five minutes and cannot be left open for someone else to hijack.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-DC-000160.caution: Applications that hold LDAP connections open without activity for more than five minutes will see them dropped and must reconnect.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000140.summary: Set the logon message title to "DoD Notice and Consent Banner", "US Department of Defense Warning Statement", or an organization-approved equivalent, so the required warning banner is clearly presented before console logon.
claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000140.caution: An organization-defined title must not contradict or alter the banner text required by WN19-SO-000130, and it will need a manual review since automated tools only look for the two standard titles.

claude-cowork-2026-09:WN19-SO-000370.summary: Enable "System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects" so shared system objects such as symbolic links get tighter default permissions, and non-administrators cannot modify objects they did not create.
